standard.name: right-censoring positivity through the analysis horizon

assumptions.condition: Every finite-part coordinate density of \(\mu_{zx}\) is bounded above by \(M\).
Every finite-part coordinate density of \(\mu_{zx}\) is \(L_{\mathrm{Lip}}\)-Lipschitz.

standard.name: positive principal-stratum mass on the target set

assumptions.condition: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed with law \(P\).
For every \(x\in\mathcal X\), \((r,t)\in\mathcal T\), and \(B\in\{[0,r],(r,\infty]\}\), the set \(\arg\min_{u\in[t,\tau]\cup\{\infty\}}F_x(u;r,t,B)\) is a singleton.

standard.name: unique optimizer on a regular value-function region

definitions.name: Truncated event-time carrier
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal E=[0,\tau]\sqcup\{\infty\}\), where \(\infty\) is isolated and maximal.

definitions.name: Conditional survivor-capacity fiber
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal N_x=\{\nu_x\in\Gamma(d_x,\zeta_x):\nu_x((u,\infty]\times B)\le K_x(u,B)\text{ for every }u\in[0,\tau]\text{ and every Borel }B\subseteq\mathcal E\}\).

definitions.name: Joint TV-SACE and RM-SACE identified set
Nested-survivor chain flow
definitions.construction: On \(\mathcal G_m\), inject each treated-readmission mass at a chain source indexed by \(j\); send chain flow across death cut \(k\) with capacity \(\kappa^x_{kj}\); allow exit \(f^x_{ij}\) to control-death demand \(i\); impose \(\sum_j f^x_{ij}=d_x(i)\) and \(\sum_i f^x_{ij}=\zeta_x(j)\).

definitions.name: Finite-grid support program
definitions.construction: \(h_m(c)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\max_f\sum_{i,j}c^x_{ij}f^x_{ij}\), where the maximization uses the chain flow; equivalently minimize \(\sum_i\alpha_i d_x(i)+\sum_j\beta_j\zeta_x(j)+\sum_{k,j}\lambda_{kj}\kappa^x_{kj}\) subject to \(\alpha_i+\beta_j+\sum_{k<i}\lambda_{kj}\ge c^x_{ij}\) and \(\lambda_{kj}\ge0\).

definitions.name: Primitive three-horizon marked-capacity exhibit
definitions.construction: Let \(\mathfrak E_3\) have \(\tau=3\), degenerate \(X\), \(Z\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) independent of all potential times, \(C=3\), death categories \((d_i^\star)_{i=0}^3=(1/2,3/2,5/2,\infty)\), treated-readmission categories \((r_j^\star)_{j=0}^3=(1/4,5/4,9/4,\infty)\), and \(R(0)=\infty\). With death rows and readmission columns, the within-arm tables are \(100\mu_0^\star=\begin{pmatrix}0&0&0&25\\0&0&0&25\\0&0&0&25\\0&0&0&25\end{pmatrix}\) and \(100\mu_1^\star=\begin{pmatrix}5&0&0&5\\5&10&0&5\\5&5&10&10\\10&5&5&20\end{pmatrix}\). Every marked survivor capacity after death cuts \(k=0,1,2\) is displayed by \(100\kappa^\star=\begin{pmatrix}20&20&15&35\\15&10&15&30\\10&5&5&20\end{pmatrix}\); the capacity for any readmission-mark set is the sum of its displayed columns. Define \(100f^-=\begin{pmatrix}10&0&10&5\\0&10&5&10\\15&5&0&5\\0&5&0&20\end{pmatrix}\) and \(100f^+=\begin{pmatrix}5&0&10&10\\10&15&0&0\\0&0&0&25\\10&5&5&5\end{pmatrix}\). Both have row sums \((25,25,25,25)\) and column sums \((25,20,15,40)\). Their complete chain-arc loads \(100(\sum_{i>k}f^-_{ij})_{kj}=\begin{pmatrix}15&20&5&35\\15&10&0&25\\0&5&0&20\end{pmatrix}\) and \(100(\sum_{i>k}f^+_{ij})_{kj}=\begin{pmatrix}20&20&5&30\\10&5&5&30\\10&5&5&5\end{pmatrix}\) are entrywise bounded by \(100\kappa^\star\). Explicit full lifts, with all unlisted entries zero, are \(100(q^-_{000},q^-_{003},q^-_{010},q^-_{022},q^-_{111},q^-_{113},q^-_{123},q^-_{132},q^-_{220},q^-_{221},q^-_{223},q^-_{230},q^-_{331},q^-_{333})=(5,5,5,10,10,5,5,5,5,5,5,10,5,20)\) and \(100(q^+_{000},q^+_{003},q^+_{013},q^+_{022},q^+_{110},q^+_{111},q^+_{120},q^+_{121},q^+_{223},q^+_{233},q^+_{330},q^+_{331},q^+_{332},q^+_{333})=(5,5,5,10,5,10,5,5,10,15,10,5,5,5)\), where \(q^\pm_{ihj}=\Pr(D(0)=d_i^\star,D(1)=d_h^\star,R(1)=r_j^\star)\); attach \(R(0)=\infty\).

definitions.name: Censoring-aware finite-sample outer set
definitions.construction: Fix \(0=a_0<\cdots<a_m=\tau\) and readmission bins \(B_j\). In cell \((z,x)\), give every observable moment \(A^{zx}_{ij}\), \(Y^{zx}_i\), and \(V^{zx}_j\) an interval centered at its empirical proportion, clipped to \([0,1]\), with radius \(\sqrt{\log(2J/\alpha)/(2N_{zx})}\) when \(N_{zx}>0\), and use \([0,1]\) when \(N_{zx}=0\). Give \(p_x\) the interval centered at \(\widehat p_x\), clipped to \([0,1]\), with radius \(\sqrt{\log(2J/\alpha)/(2n)}\). Define \(\mathscr E_n\) as the event on which all these primitive intervals cover simultaneously. Define \(\mathcal B_n\) as all tuples of probability tables \(\pi^{zx}_{ij},\pi^{zx}_{\infty j}\), covariate masses \(p_x\), censoring vectors \(g^{zx}_i\), and candidate observable moments \(A^{zx}_{ij},Y^{zx}_i,V^{zx}_j\) such that every candidate lies in its corresponding interval, the table obeys simplex and event-order restrictions, and, for every \((z,x,i,j)\), \(g^{zx}_{i+1}\pi^{zx}_{ij}\le A^{zx}_{ij}\le g^{zx}_i\pi^{zx}_{ij}\), \(Y^{zx}_i=g^{zx}_i\{\sum_{h\ge i,j}\pi^{zx}_{hj}+\sum_j\pi^{zx}_{\infty j}\}\), \(V^{zx}_j=g^{zx}_m\pi^{zx}_{\infty j}\), and \(1\ge g^{zx}_0\ge\cdots\ge g^{zx}_m\ge\gamma\). For a discrete exact-death grid replace the first pair of inequalities by \(A^{zx}_{ij}=g^{zx}_i\pi^{zx}_{ij}\). Define \(\mathcal C_n\) as the union of the exact chain-flow surface images over \(\mathcal B_n\).

definitions.name: Marked-process multiplier-band handle
definitions.construction: \(\mathscr H_{\mathrm{MB}}\) starts from one joint counting-process martingale representation for the marked readmission, death, and estimated-censoring primitive vector through \(\tau\); it then composes increment-level multipliers with the active deadline cut \(u_x^\star\) and the quotient map defining \(\theta_\nu\), and integrates the resulting TV process for \(\rho_\nu\).

statements.statement: For every bounded measurable \(g:\mathcal E^2\to\mathbb R\), \(\int g\,d\mu_{zx}=E_P[\Delta g(D,R)/G_{zx}(L)\mid Z=z,X=x]\). Hence the complete truncated within-arm laws \(\mu_{zx}\), including the horizon atom, are functionals of \(P\).
statements.justification: This standard IPCW recovery lemma records why every future-death resource in the marked capacity is an observed-law functional under full-horizon follow-up.
statements.gap: This is a cited standard right-censoring identity anchored to Goldberg (2019), not a novelty claim; its marked complete-path specialization fixes the primitive input to the capacity theorem.
statements.consumer: It makes the sharp capacity operational after the pancreatic-cancer application passes its arm-specific follow-up audit through \(\tau\).

statements.statement: The complete joint identified set of standardized TV-SACE and RM-SACE surfaces is exactly \(\Theta_I(P)\). Necessity holds because \(D(0)>u\) implies \(D(1)>u\) under terminal monotonicity. Conversely, every measurable family \(\nu_x\in\mathcal N_x\) admits a measurable full-law lift of \((D(0),R(0),D(1),R(1))\) that preserves both \(\mu_{0x}\) and \(\mu_{1x}\), satisfies \(D(0)\le D(1)\), and reproduces \(P\).
statements.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: it replaces a parametric latent frailty with the exact nonparametric fiber and proves sharpness for the whole surface, not isolated coordinates.
statements.gap: Comment et al. define the surface but parameterize its cross-world law; Chen, Cui, and Yang bound a fixed scalar survivor outcome; generic transport results do not prove the marked conditional projection or full-law lift.
statements.consumer: It gives clinicians every conclusion about the complete TV-SACE/RM-SACE surface that follows from treatment exchangeability, full follow-up support, and audited terminal monotonicity alone.

statements.statement: On any ordered grid \(\mathcal G_m\), \(f^x\) belongs to \(\mathcal N_x\) if and only if it is feasible for the nested-survivor chain flow, equivalently if \(\sum_{i>k}f^x_{ij}\le\kappa^x_{kj}\) for every \(k,j\) together with its two margins. The network has \(O(m^2)\) nodes and arcs when both time axes have \(m\) levels, every feasible flow lifts to a full law, and \(h_m(c)\) equals the stated node-potential dual for every signed cost \(c\).
statements.justification: The quadratic reduction makes exact joint-surface support computation possible and exposes the complete capacity constraints rather than hiding them in a four-time table.
statements.gap: Russell and Ober-Reynolds provide generic latent-law programs and duals; neither source gives this nested chain, its complete suffix cuts, or the reconstruction of full semicompeting-risk laws.
statements.consumer: It supplies an exact auditable algorithm for the finite-horizon grids used in the Comment et al. analysis and a certificate for every reported support endpoint.

statements.statement: For each fixed \(t\) and cell \(x\), the sharp extrema of \(\nu_x(D(0)>t,R(1)\le r)\) are \(A^L_x(r,t)\) and \(A^U_x(r,t)\). One coupling attains \(A^U_x(r,t)\) simultaneously for every \(r\le t\), and another coupling attains \(A^L_x(r,t)\) simultaneously for every \(r\le t\). Therefore the standardized coordinate bounds follow by summing with weights \(p_x/S(t)\), and the sharp RM-SACE interval is obtained by integrating the opposite common TV-SACE envelopes along that fixed cohort.
statements.justification: Coordinatewise sharpness does not justify integration; common extremizers are the missing mathematical reason that fixed-cohort RM-SACE envelope integration is exact.
statements.gap: Chen, Cui, and Yang integrate threshold bounds for a scalar survivor outcome, while the opened papers do not prove one coupling jointly attains all readmission thresholds for a nested survivor cohort.
statements.consumer: It gives a closed-form RM-SACE sensitivity region without solving a new optimization problem at every integration point.

statements.statement:
In \(\mathfrak E_3\), the two arrays \(q^-_{ihj}\) and \(q^+_{ihj}\) are nonnegative, have \((D(0),R(1))\) margins \(f^-\) and \(f^+\), have \((D(1),R(1))\) margin \(\mu_1^\star\), and put mass only on \(D(0)\le D(1)\); with \(R(0)=\infty\), each is therefore a feasible full-law lift preserving both displayed within-arm tables. The displayed row sums, column sums, and complete chain-load matrices certify every marked-capacity constraint. The exact coordinate intervals are \(	heta_
u(1,1)\in[1/15,4/15]\), \(	heta_
u(2,2)\in[1/10,1/2]\), and \(	heta_
u(3,3)\in[1/5,4/5]\). For an arbitrary feasible \(f_{ij}\), \(\ell_\star(
u)=f_{10}-f_{21}+f_{30}+f_{32}\), \(\ell_\star(
u)\le f_{10}+f_{30}+f_{32}\le\kappa^\star_{00}+\kappa^\star_{22}=1/4\), while \(f_{21}+f_{31}\le1/10\) and \(f_{30}+f_{31}+f_{32}=1/4-f_{33}\ge1/20\) imply \(\ell_\star(
u)\ge-1/20\). The arrays \(q^-_{ihj}\) and \(q^+_{ihj}\) attain these two endpoints, so the sharp interval is \([-1/20,1/4]\), strictly inside the coordinate rectangle \([-3/20,7/20]\). Replacing each finite atom by a sufficiently narrow separated symmetric bump and using a common bump draw when the two death categories agree yields a bounded-Lipschitz law satisfying all maintained conditions with the same strict separation; the separation persists on a relatively open neighborhood.
statements.justification: A robust strict example establishes that the joint surface theorem adds identifying content beyond a collection of exact pointwise intervals.
statements.gap: Generic warnings that pointwise sharp bounds need not be jointly sharp do not give a legal semicompeting-risk region with binding survivor capacities and exact support certificates.
statements.consumer: It tells applied users when horizon-by-horizon uncertainty bands are mathematically incompatible and can reverse conclusions about signed clinical summaries.

statements.statement: For fixed identified within-arm margins, \(\Theta_I(P)\) is compact and convex in the uniform norm on \(\mathcal H_\eta\), every continuous signed support functional is attained, and the interpolated exact grid surface sets from nested meshes converge to \(\Theta_I(P)\) in Hausdorff distance. Consequently their support values and sharp fixed-cohort RM integrals converge to the continuous-support values.
statements.justification: Continuous-time conclusions require more than solving unrelated finite grids; compactness and Hausdorff convergence transfer exact support certificates to the scientific time scale.
statements.gap: Generic optimal-transport consistency does not address strict within-arm event order, a nested survivor denominator, or uniform convergence of a two-index surface image.
statements.consumer: It justifies refining the clinical horizon grid without changing the estimand or losing sharpness.

statements.statement: For every deterministic finite grid and \(0<\alpha<1\), conditional Hoeffding inequalities within each nonempty treatment--covariate cell and the unconditional Hoeffding inequalities for \(\widehat p_x\) give \(\inf_P\Pr_P(\mathscr E_n)\ge1-\alpha\). On the single simultaneous event \(\mathscr E_n\), arm-specific independent censoring implies that the true coarsened primitive vector satisfies \(g^{zx}_{i+1}\pi^{zx}_{ij}\le A^{zx}_{ij}\le g^{zx}_i\pi^{zx}_{ij}\), \(Y^{zx}_i=g^{zx}_i\{\sum_{h\ge i,j}\pi^{zx}_{hj}+\sum_j\pi^{zx}_{\infty j}\}\), \(V^{zx}_j=g^{zx}_m\pi^{zx}_{\infty j}\), and \(1\ge g^{zx}_0\ge\cdots\ge g^{zx}_m\ge\gamma\); hence it belongs to \(\mathcal B_n\) and deterministically \(\Theta_I(P)|_{\mathcal G_m}\subseteq\mathcal C_n\). Therefore \(\inf_P\Pr_P\{\Theta_I(P)|_{\mathcal G_m}\subseteq\mathcal C_n\}\ge1-\alpha\). The result uses sample size \(n\) for \(p_x\), assigns \([0,1]\) to every primitive interval in a zero-count cell, and remains valid at every change of the active flow face.
statements.justification: A face-robust finite-sample guard is the honest fallback wherever the sharp endpoint map is nondifferentiable and ordinary multiplier calibration is invalid.
statements.gap: Goldberg controls individual IPCW averages and Cho--Russell give asymptotic perturbed-LP inference; neither propagates one joint censoring-moment event through every nested-survivor surface face.
statements.consumer: It provides conservative but auditable uncertainty sets for the finite clinical horizon grid even when active cuts tie.

statements.statement: If \(D(0)=D(1)\) almost surely, then every \(\nu_x\in\mathcal N_x\) satisfies \(\nu_x(D(0)>t,R(1)\le r)=\mu_{1x}(D(1)>t,R(1)\le r)\), so \(\Theta_I(P)\) is a singleton equal to the ordinary standardized difference of within-arm cumulative incidences among the common survivor cohort.
statements.justification: The reduction checks that the capacity theorem collapses to the familiar identified survivor contrast when treatment has no terminal effect.
statements.gap: This is a required sanity reduction rather than a novelty claim.
statements.consumer: It supplies a diagnostic implementation test and interpretable benchmark for applied users.

statements.statement: Can the handle \(\mathscr H_{\mathrm{MB}}\) be completed to prove a joint asymptotic-linear expansion and functional central limit theorem for the estimated marked arm laws and censoring survival through \(\tau\), such that the unique-cut derivative and a mesh \(o(n^{-1/2})\) condition yield conditionally consistent simultaneous multiplier bands for every lower and upper TV-SACE and RM-SACE endpoint on \(\mathcal T\)?
statements.justification: This is the first-class unresolved content: it turns sharp population surfaces into simultaneous frequentist statements while exposing the full-horizon censoring and grid-bias bottlenecks.
statements.gap: Bluhmki et al. handle smooth multivariate Nelson--Aalen processes, and Fang--Santos, Firpo--Galvao--Parker, and Cho--Russell handle nonsmooth optimized maps after a primitive limit; no opened result supplies their required composition here.
statements.consumer: It would deliver simultaneous coverage for the clinically interpreted curves in Comment et al. on regions where the active survivor deadline is stable.

sampling_model.design: Observational or randomized binary treatment with conditional exchangeability and i.i.d. superpopulation sampling.
sampling_model.units: Each unit supplies baseline \(X\), treatment \(Z\), at-risk history, first readmission history, terminal-event history, and administrative censoring through \(\tau\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every supported covariate cell has positive mass and both treatment arms have positive probability.
sampling_model.censoring: Within each realized arm \(z\), \(C\) is conditionally independent of that arm's pair \((D(z),R(z))\) given \(X\), and \(G_{zx}(u)\ge\gamma\) through \(\tau\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Marked product-limit or IPCW estimation of \(\mu_{zx}\), \(G_{zx}\), and \(p_x\); the multiplier expansion remains the open inference node.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Defines two-index TV-SACE and RM-SACE and estimates them by posterior imputation under parametric illness--death frailty models.
Theorem 3.1 gives sharp fixed-time SACE bounds by integrating pointwise symbolic linear-program bounds.
Theorem 7 characterizes existence of a probability measure with prescribed marginals under support inequalities.
Characterizes sharp bounds for continuous functionals of latent joint potential-outcome laws through random-set inequalities and linear programs.
Represents generic known-marginal causal partial-identification problems by multi-marginal optimal transport and proves rates for selected quadratic costs.
Derives partial-identification bounds for semi-competing-risk effects under a single population stratification.
Bootstraps randomly perturbed finite linear-program values to obtain uniformly valid inference for linear-moment identified sets.
Proves conditional weak convergence of an increment-level wild bootstrap for multivariate Nelson--Aalen processes under censoring.
Establishes derivative-based valid resampling for directionally differentiable maps when the ordinary bootstrap fails.
Develops uniform resampling for optimized value functions using estimated directional derivatives.
Sharpens scalar SACE bounds with detailed survival histories and ranked-average-score restrictions while indexing cross-world survival dependence by a copula parameter.
Represents sharp bounds on functionals of the joint potential-outcome distribution as optimal-transport values and estimates them through the dual.
Derives central-limit and Hoeffding-type results for inverse-probability-of-censoring-weighted estimators under right censoring.

tldr: Death truncates readmission, so the two-index TV-SACE and RM-SACE surfaces depend on an unidentified cross-world assignment of treated readmission times to control survival times. Under arm-specific independent censoring through the full horizon and terminal-survival monotonicity, the proposal characterizes the complete sharp surface by a necessary-and-sufficient marked-capacity lift, proves common fixed-cohort extremizers and exact RM integration, and gives a fully certified three-horizon law whose joint cross-cohort support is strictly narrower than its coordinate rectangle. Quadratic chain flows, continuous support convergence, and one-event finite-sample outer containment make the characterization operational. The genuinely open step is a joint marked-product-limit/IPCW functional limit and unique-cut multiplier theorem for simultaneous regular-region bands.

project_justification.gap: Comment et al. define clinically meaningful TV-SACE and RM-SACE surfaces but close the latent four-time law parametrically. Existing SACE bounds are scalar or fixed-stratum, and generic random-set or optimal-transport methods do not expose the nested readmission-marked survival constraints or joint horizon compatibility.
project_justification.niche: Terminal monotonicity turns every always-survivor cohort into a nested resource-selection problem. Conditioning the death-order coupling on the treated readmission mark creates a capacity object with exact cuts, sparse flows, and common fixed-cohort extrema.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies the if-and-only-if capacity image, constructive full-law sharpness, common extremizers, an explicit primitive separation certificate, exact computation and continuous approximation, conservative one-event finite-sample uncertainty, and a sharply isolated route to simultaneous multiplier inference.

related_work: Comment, Mealli, Haneuse, and Zigler (2025) define TV-SACE and RM-SACE and estimate them with a Bayesian illness--death frailty model; their setup and clinical motivation are the writing exemplar, while the present identified set leaves the cross-world law nonparametric. Yang and Ding (2018) use detailed survival histories and copula sensitivity for scalar SACE bounds, which motivates exploiting the full death-time law but does not determine a nested compatible surface. Nevo and Gorfine (2022) derive semi-competing-risk bounds for a single population stratification, not changing always-survivor cohorts. Chen, Cui, and Yang (2024) transform fixed-time SACE fractional programs into symbolic linear programs and integrate tail bounds; their estimator construction is methodologically adjacent but does not establish common surface extremizers. Strassen (1965) supplies the stochastic-order coupling theorem adapted in the measurable lift. Russell (2021) and Ober-Reynolds (2023) motivate sharp latent-law support programs and duality, while the proposed chain reduction uses the special nested order. Goldberg (2019) supplies standard IPCW recovery and concentration tools under right censoring; the displayed complete-path identity is a cited lemma rather than a proposed advance. Cho and Russell (2024), Bluhmki et al. (2019), Fang and Santos (2019), and Firpo, Galvao, and Parker (2023) inform the inference route without being claimed as results extended by the settled theorems.
technical_internal_limitation: The finite-sample outer set is guaranteed to contain the truth at a deterministic grid, but a quantitative shrinking rate under simultaneous grid refinement is not yet a theorem. At tied deadline cuts the sharp endpoint map is only directionally differentiable; the ordinary centered multiplier bootstrap is not asserted to be valid there. Full-horizon censoring support is essential because an endpoint for an early survivor cohort can depend on treated death information later than that cohort horizon.
honest_scope: The IPCW recovery identity is a standard cited lemma. The necessary-and-sufficient capacity projection, measurable full-law lifting, chain-flow equivalence, common fixed-cohort extremizers, primitive strict cross-cohort support certificate, compact continuous image, qualitative grid convergence, and finite-grid outer containment are proposed as results to prove. The joint marked-process functional central limit theorem, estimated-censoring remainder control, simultaneous multiplier validity, and root-\(n\)-negligible grid bias remain explicit open content. No claim is made under censoring positivity restricted only to the target horizon, for recurrent readmissions, or at multiple active cuts.

seed_details.anchor_location: Sections 1, 2.2, 2.4--2.6, and 5 of the published article; Equation (2) for TV-SACE and the posterior full-potential-outcome imputation construction.
seed_details.anchor_read: The paper motivates nested always-survivor cohorts, defines the two-index TV-SACE and RM-SACE surfaces, and obtains their posterior by a parametric illness--death model with a shared gamma frailty. Its conclusion identifies frailty and baseline-hazard specification as substantive limitations.
seed_details.kernel: Prove that the entire standardized TV-SACE and RM-SACE surface is the image of conditional couplings \(\nu_x=\mathcal L(D(0),R(1)\mid X=x)\) satisfying readmission-marked survivor-capacity inequalities, and prove the converse by a measurable conditional quantile lift to a full four-potential-time law.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first unresolved step after Comment et al. is to replace posterior imputation of the cross-world law by an if-and-only-if observed-law fiber and to show that projection loses no full-law compatibility information.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: this is immediate from Strassen because terminal monotonicity is just stochastic order. Rebuttal: ordinary terminal stochastic order omits the inequalities as measures in treated readmission time; the theorem must derive their necessity, disintegrate them conditional on the readmission mark, and measurably restore both within-arm joint margins.

seed_details.anchor_location: Theorem 7 and the stochastic-domination application in Section 6; the proof uses separation to turn set inequalities into existence of a coupling.
seed_details.anchor_read: Strassen characterizes existence of probability measures with prescribed marginals and support restrictions, but does not exploit the Ferrers structure generated by ordered death deadlines and nested survivor cohorts.
seed_details.kernel: Specialize the complete event-set inequalities to an exact \(O(m^2)\) chain flow, derive its support dual, and prove that greedy prefix and suffix matchings produce common CDF extremizers for every readmission threshold within a fixed survivor cohort.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed proof step is to replace generic separating sets by suffix cuts in a Ferrers matching network, then prove simultaneous prefix attainment by the augmentation property rather than optimize each threshold separately.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for nested survivor flow, TV-SACE transport, common SACE extremizers, and readmission-specific coupling cuts found generic random-set and optimal-transport programs but no chain reduction or common-extremizer theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: this is a routine min-cost-flow encoding of a transportation table. Rebuttal: the nonroutine content is completeness of the marked suffix cuts and one full-law extremizer attaining all readmission-prefix ranks, which is exactly what makes RM integration sharp and distinguishes joint surface support from pointwise rectangles.

seed_details.anchor_location: Sections 4 and 5, where posterior surface summaries are reported and misspecification produces bias and undercoverage.
seed_details.anchor_read: The applied analysis treats complete TV-SACE and RM-SACE curves as the clinical object, but supplies Bayesian credible intervals under a parametric frailty law rather than simultaneous frequentist inference for a sharp nonparametric surface.
seed_details.kernel: Derive a joint marked product-limit/IPCW functional central limit theorem through \(\tau\), compose it with the unique-cut derivative, and validate multiplier bands for TV-SACE and RM-SACE on regular compact regions.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed proof step from Bluhmki et al. is to obtain one influence expansion for jointly marked readmission, death, and estimated-censoring moments before applying an optimizer derivative; the first changed step from Fang--Santos is to establish the missing primitive process limit rather than assume it.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing TV-SACE or nested SACE surfaces with multiplier bands, product-limit processes, and directional derivatives returned no exact result; the closest papers cover smooth Nelson--Aalen processes or generic optimized values separately.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: generic directional-delta and wild-bootstrap theorems already give these bands. Rebuttal: neither literature supplies the full-horizon estimated-censoring expansion for the jointly marked primitive vector, the uniform unique-cut chain rule, or a grid-bias condition for this surface.

seed_details.anchor_location: The standard, data-dependent, and uniform IPCW Hoeffding inequalities in Sections 3--5.
seed_details.kernel: Construct a joint right-censoring moment region and propagate it through every active face of the finite-grid capacity polytope to obtain honest finite-sample outer coverage of the full surface.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: union-bound each IPCW cell and run an LP. Rebuttal: shared estimated censoring and random risk denominators require one feasible primitive region, and containment must hold uniformly over changing faces; the basic guard is credible but quantitative shrinking is not yet closed.
seed_details.disposition: dropped after ranking because the strongest current result is conservative containment and the shrinking-rate theorem remains secondary to the capacity kernel

seed_details.anchor_location: The recurrent-event principal-stratum estimand and shared-frailty construction in Sections 2--3.
seed_details.kernel: Characterize sharp cumulative-count SACE surfaces by path/death couplings satisfying increasing-cylinder survivor capacities, with a finite-grid flow or a theorem locating the exact obstruction to the first-event chain reduction.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: replace first-event indicators by counts and reuse the same transport proof. Rebuttal: recurrent paths are only partially ordered by all increasing cylinders, so the first-event suffix reduction fails without a new path-space coupling theorem; that same difficulty makes feasibility materially lower for a first version.
seed_details.disposition: dropped after ranking because the path-space sufficiency direction lacks a verified finite structural reduction

seed_details.anchor_location: Sections 3--4 on survival-history sharpening and copula-indexed cross-world survival sensitivity.
seed_details.kernel: Relax every readmission-marked survivor-capacity inequality by a common violation budget \(\delta\), derive surface support functions \(h_\delta\), and characterize the smallest \(\delta^\star\) at which a prespecified RM-SACE sign conclusion fails.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: this is only right-hand-side sensitivity analysis for a linear program. Rebuttal: a useful version needs a closed cutwise critical value shared across a continuum surface, and current evidence does not yet show that the common budget has a clinically defensible calibration.
seed_details.disposition: dropped after ranking because the violation metric is not yet substantively anchored

seed_details.anchor_location: Sections 2--3 on a single event-order principal stratification and its partial-identification bounds.
seed_details.kernel: Give necessary and sufficient conditions under which a surface of nested always-survivor effects can be represented by one fixed semi-competing-risk stratum, and prove robust non-representability outside that region.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: the estimands plainly condition on different populations. Rebuttal: an exact equivalence frontier could still be informative, but the likely condition collapses to no treatment effect on survival, making the advance too close to a definitional observation.
seed_details.disposition: dropped because the novelty rebuttal collapses to a restrictive known special case

seed_details.anchor_location: The optimal-transport dual formulation and plug-in estimation results in Sections 2--4.
seed_details.kernel: Derive a sharp mesh-dependent Hausdorff rate for nested-survivor surface sets and an adaptive grid whose optimization and discretization errors balance uniformly over signed support directions.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: bounded-Lipschitz margins make the grid error immediately \(O(\Delta)\). Rebuttal: changing cut locations and quotient standardization complicate uniform support convergence, but without a matching lower bound or adaptive complexity theorem the seed is ancillary.
seed_details.disposition: dropped as an ancillary numerical-analysis result

seed_details.anchor_location: The clinical decision motivation in the Introduction and the utility-function extension proposed in the Conclusion.
seed_details.kernel: Choose treatment by maximizing worst-case utility integrated over TV-SACE and survival, and prove regret bounds relative to the oracle policy over the capacity-identified welfare set.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: the utility weights and policy class, rather than the data, determine the conclusion. Rebuttal: a rigorous minimax rule could be valuable, but the present topic does not supply a defensible utility class or a policy-learning sample structure.
seed_details.disposition: dropped because the decision object is not sufficiently specified

threads: Comment et al. (2025), Sections 2.2 and 2.4--2.6, define the destination surfaces and impute the cross-world law through a parametric frailty model.

Chen, Cui, and Yang (2024), Theorem 3.1 and Appendix A.4, obtain sharp fixed-time scalar SACE bounds by converting a fractional program to symbolic linear programs and integrating pointwise tail bounds.
Nevo and Gorfine (2022), Sections 2--3, obtain bounds for a single event-order stratification rather than the nested always-survivor cohorts indexed by \(t\).

Gao, Ge, and Qian (2024), Sections 1--3, characterize generic known-marginal causal bounds by multi-marginal optimal transport and analyze selected quadratic costs; they do not eliminate the four-time law to a readmission-marked capacity.
literature_map.occupancy_conclusion: The scalar and generic transport problems are occupied, but no opened source gives an if-and-only-if projection of the full TV-SACE/RM-SACE surface or a measurable full-law lift from \(\nu_x\).

threads: Strassen (1965), Theorem 7, supplies the coupling-existence separation theorem from which conditional stochastic-order lifts can be adapted.

Russell (2021), Theorems 1--2 and the computational appendix, uses random-set inequalities and linear programming for sharp joint-potential-outcome functionals without a nested-survivor chain reduction.
Ober-Reynolds (2023), Sections 2--4, gives optimal-transport values and dual estimators for joint potential outcomes but no readmission-indexed survivor capacities.
Chen, Cui, and Yang (2024), Appendix A.4, integrates separately optimized threshold bounds; it does not prove that one coupling attains all thresholds within a survivor cohort.
literature_map.occupancy_conclusion: Generic coupling, random-set, and transport programs are settled tools; the complete suffix-cut family, quadratic network, and common fixed-cohort CDF extremizers remain unoccupied in the searched literature.

threads: Bluhmki et al. (2019), Lemma 1 and the conditional weak-convergence theorem, preserve multivariate Nelson--Aalen covariance with increment-level multipliers under censoring.
Fang and Santos (2019), Theorems 3.1--3.2, show why ordinary bootstrap inference fails for nondifferentiable maps and replace it by estimated directional derivatives.
Firpo, Galvao, and Parker (2023), Sections 3--4, give uniform resampling for optimized value functions after a primitive process limit is available.

Cho and Russell (2024), Sections 3.1--3.3, perturb finite linear-program values under generic-basis stability; their primitives are finite linear moments rather than jointly marked censored event processes.
literature_map.occupancy_conclusion: The two required halves exist separately, but no source composes a full-horizon marked product-limit/IPCW process with the continuum cut map for simultaneous TV-SACE/RM-SACE bands.
